# Change review CHG-3104: tag routes to the upstream (NET-2104)

Our upstream **up1** (AS 65200) now requires the BGP community **65200:100** ("customer of AS 65200, announce to your customers") on every route we send them, and will stop re-announcing untagged routes next week. A colleague's change, in their words: "Added the 65200:100 tag to the TO-UPSTREAM route-map. Sessions are up, nothing else touched."

Your job is to decide whether this change may be applied to production in tonight's window. The change is already applied to `configs/edge1.conf` in this folder; [PROPOSED.diff](PROPOSED.diff) shows it against production.

- Don't rewrite the change. If it is wrong, say why; the author will fix it.
- Don't edit `CHECKS.md`. It lists the network team's checks.
- Base the decision on evidence from testing the change in the lab (`topology.clab.yml`, a containerlab topology of this part of the network), and include the evidence.

frr defaults datacenter
hostname edge1
!
interface lo
 ip address 192.0.2.1/32
!
interface eth1
 description cust1 (customer, AS 65100)
 ip address 10.0.1.1/30
!
interface eth2
 description up1 (upstream transit, AS 65200)
 ip address 10.0.2.1/30
!
interface eth3
 description peer1 (settlement-free peer, AS 65300)
 ip address 10.0.3.1/30
!
ip route 192.0.2.0/24 blackhole
!
! Prefixes the customer may announce to us
ip prefix-list CUSTOMER-IN seq 10 permit 10.100.0.0/24
!
! Prefixes we announce to the upstream and the peer: our block and our customer's
ip prefix-list OUR-ROUTES seq 10 permit 192.0.2.0/24
ip prefix-list OUR-ROUTES seq 20 permit 10.100.0.0/24
!
route-map CUSTOMER-IN permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list CUSTOMER-IN
 set local-preference 200
!
route-map UPSTREAM-IN permit 10
 set local-preference 100
!
route-map PEER-IN permit 10
 set local-preference 150
!
route-map TO-CUSTOMER permit 10
!
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list OUR-ROUTES
 set extcommunity rt 65200:100
!
route-map TO-PEER permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list OUR-ROUTES
!
router bgp 65000
 bgp router-id 192.0.2.1
 neighbor 10.0.1.2 remote-as 65100
 neighbor 10.0.1.2 description cust1
 neighbor 10.0.2.2 remote-as 65200
 neighbor 10.0.2.2 description up1
 neighbor 10.0.3.2 remote-as 65300
 neighbor 10.0.3.2 description peer1
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.0.2.0/24
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 route-map CUSTOMER-IN in
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 route-map TO-CUSTOMER out
  neighbor 10.0.2.2 route-map UPSTREAM-IN in
  neighbor 10.0.2.2 route-map TO-UPSTREAM out
  neighbor 10.0.3.2 route-map PEER-IN in
  neighbor 10.0.3.2 route-map TO-PEER out
 exit-address-family
!

content.text: The author used `set extcommunity rt` (an extended community route-target), but the checks require a **standard** BGP community `65200:100`. Correct syntax would be `set community 65200:100`. Let me run the dry-run to confirm.

The dry-run confirms it: verdict is **DO NOT APPLY THIS CHANGE**. The two TICKET checks fail — up1 sees the routes but with no communities. The author used `set extcommunity rt 65200:100` which attaches an extended-community route-target, not a standard BGP community. FRR's `set extcommunity rt` does not populate the standard communities attribute, so up1 receives the routes with `communities none`. The correct syntax would be `set community 65200:100`. All 5 GUARD and 5 LEAK GUARD checks pass, so the sessions and leak controls are fine; the change simply doesn't do what the ticket requires.
